item.dc:creator: rod

Science made simple.
Results made real.

Combined Science, Biology, Chemistry and Physics for Years 9 to 11. Is science stressing out your child?

  • Have they been placed into a foundation science class but need grade 6s for college?
  • Unsure which exam board they are following? Or which course?
  • Have they experienced inconsistent teaching due to staff absence?
  • Former Head of Science — 20+ years teaching
  • Leeds & West Yorkshire in person
  • Anywhere in the UK online
  • Y9-Y11 GCSE Science specialist

One platform for science tutoring and STEM activities.

SMARTinSCIENCE was set up by Rod Martin in 2026 to bring together his tutoring and STEM businesses into one platform. Rod has been teaching Science for over 20 years in England and continues to teach part-time in Leeds — focussing on Years 9 to 11.

Rod has a wealth of experience in curriculum design and teaching & learning. His positive attitude has supported thousands of children through their Science GCSEs, and because he still teaches part-time in Yorkshire he is very aware of how to support students through their science exams.

More about Rod →

Three sciences, and the skills that carry the marks

Embedding exam technique within all lessons.

Biology

Chemistry

Physics

Working Scientifically

Two things worth knowing first

There is one National Science Curriculum in England & Wales and four exam boards examining it. Which board your child sits, and which course they are on, changes how they should revise.

Which exam board?

AQA, Edexcel, OCR or Eduqas. The content is the same, but each board organises it differently and writes its papers differently — so knowing which one is vital for exam preparation.

Combined or separate?

Most students take Combined Science and come away with two GCSEs; a smaller number take Biology, Chemistry and Physics separately. Both routes are catered for, with bolt-on sessions through the year.

A fun, accessible way to excel at GCSE sciences

SMARTin SCIENCE offers Y9-Y11 students a fun, accessible way to build confidence and excel in their GCSE science exams. Using a combination of engaging science education with a supportive structured approach, we make complex topics easier and help students connect with the material.

Our vision is to empower students through an enjoyable, relatable approach to science, helping them confidently advance their knowledge and exam readiness. That includes a commitment to simplifying challenging concepts and creating an environment where students feel both challenged and supported.

Four Weeks. Three sciences. One confident student.

Small group classes — enough for discussion and shared learning, small enough that nobody hides at the back. A structured, pacy, genuinely enjoyable confidence boost, built and taught by a former Head of Science.

Biology

The topics students most often confuse, organised into clear comparisons — cells, infection, organisation, homeostasis and the required practicals.

Chemistry

Atomic structure, bonding, moles and electrolysis — the periodic table's key rules, and balancing equations until it is automatic.

Physics

Energy, forces, waves and electricity — choosing the right equation, rearranging it accurately and reading the data behind it.

Exam technique

The session that improves grades fastest: command words, a structure for 6-mark questions, timed past papers and a personal revision plan.

  • Different interactive activities throughout every session
  • Short videos to watch between sessions to consolidate learning
  • Home Learning set, marked and returned – with feedback that reaches you, not just your child
  • The same four phases every week, so students always know what is coming next

See the four weeks in full → Dates & times

STEM Workshops, Afterschool Clubs and Holiday Clubs

Whether a child needs science support or simply wants to delve deeper into STEM, we provide opportunities to learn beyond the curriculum.

STEM workshops

One-off, hands-on sessions for a class, a year group or a community group — practical science with a proper question behind it.

After-school clubs

A weekly science club through term time, where the keen get stretched and the quiet ones get pulled back in.

Holiday clubs

Longer blocks in half term and the school holidays — time for the messier experiments that never fit a lesson.

See workshops & clubs →

Sessions are led by Rod Martin

Rod is a highly experienced science teacher, tutor, and former Head of Science with over two decades of teaching experience. During that time, he has watched countless bright students lose confidence in science, often because a single topic moved too quickly and left them struggling to understand what came next.

Everything parents usually ask

Y9, Y10 and Y11 students sitting GCSE Science. It suits students who are capable but have lost confidence, students who have fallen behind after missing topics, and students who understand the content but keep losing marks in exams.

Sooner than most parents expect, because the first thing that shifts is not knowledge but approach — reading the command word, showing the working, structuring a longer answer. Those habits start paying back within a few sessions and they carry into every paper afterwards.

How long the whole thing runs depends on the student. Some want a short, focused block before an exam; others keep a weekly session going through Year 10 and 11. Ask and Rod will tell you honestly what he thinks yours needs.

The core content of GCSE Combined Science is shared across AQA, Edexcel, OCR and Eduqas, and that is what the course teaches. Tell me your child's board when you enquire and the practice questions and past papers used will support it.

Yes. Homework is marked and returned, and progress feedback comes to you — not just to your child. You'll know what improved and what still needs work.

item.title: About page
item.dc:creator: rod
item.content:encoded:
Twenty years of watching students decide they're "not a science person".

They almost always are. SMARTin SCIENCE exists to prove it — in four weeks.

Rod Martin

Expert Science Tutor · Former Head of Science

  • Over 20 years of teaching experience
  • Former Head of Science in a UK secondary school
  • Biology, Chemistry and Physics to GCSE level
  • GCSE Sciences specialist for Y9-Y11
  • Whole-department experience of how papers are marked
  • Sessions built around confidence, not just content

From the front of the classroom

Rod Martin has spent over twenty years teaching science in UK schools, including running an entire science department as Head of Science. In that time, he has taught every part of the Science specifications to every kind of student — the ones who love it, the ones who dread it, and the very large group in between who simply lost the thread somewhere in Year 9.

That last group is the reason SMARTin SCIENCE exists.

Twenty years of it

  • 20+ years of science teaching experience
  • Continues to achieve above national pass rates in science
  • Regularly standardises and moderates science exam papers — so knows what answers are expected
  • Teaches all the GCSE science curriculums (Combined Science, Biology, Chemistry and Physics) to Higher tier
  • 7 years in charge of a large science department — first as Head of Science, then as Assistant Headteacher in charge of science & data
  • Former Lead Practitioner for Teaching and Learning — has guided and supported newly qualified teachers into the profession

Why four weeks

Long tutoring arrangements can drift. A fixed four-week course does not. Each week has one job — Biology, Chemistry, Physics, then exam technique — and every session ends with the student able to name something they can now do that they couldn't do an hour earlier.

Four weeks is also long enough to change habits: how to read a command word, how to structure a six-mark answer, how to rearrange an equation without panicking. Those habits carry into every paper afterwards, which is why the effect outlasts the course.

Knowing where the marks actually go

Having taught the specification and led a department, Rod knows exactly where students lose marks — and it is rarely where parents assume. It's the "explain" answered as a "describe". The unit left off. The graph not fully annotated. The six-marker that contains all the right science in no usable order.

These are fixable in weeks, not years. That's what week four is for.

The three values behind every session

  • Empowerment — students leave able to do the thing themselves, not just watch it be done.
  • Engagement — if a session is boring, it isn't working. Activities, comparisons and real examples do the heavy lifting.
  • Excellence — high expectations, clearly explained, with the support to actually meet them.

Leeds in person, England and Wales online

In-person sessions run across Leeds. Everywhere else in England and Wales, the same course runs online — same worksheets, same homework, same feedback.

See where Rod teaches →

Contact Rod to secure your place

Is science stressing your teen? In four weeks I'll give them knowledge and confidence to put them back on track with their GCSE Science.

item.title: Course page
item.dc:creator: rod
item.content:encoded:
Four Weeks. Three sciences. One confident student.

A structured, fast, genuinely enjoyable confidence boost for students sitting GCSE Science — built and taught by a former Head of Science with over 20 years in the classroom.

Designed for students who no longer believe they can succeed in science

The one who is overwhelmed

Three sciences, one exam series, and no idea where to start. We replace the panic with a plan, then work through it a week at a time.

The one with gaps in knowledge

Missed a run of lessons or had copious supply teachers, and nothing since has quite made sense. We find the topic where the issues began and rebuild it from there.

The one who knows the knowledge but loses the 'simple' marks

Understands the science, still drops grades in the exam. Could be a command-word problem or a Working Scientifically issue. This is very fixable.

What happens in each of the four weeks

Each week is self-contained but builds on the last. By week four, the science is familiar and the exam is just a format.

Biology — that actually sticks!

The topics students most often confuse, organised into clear, memorable comparisons.

  • Cell biology, transport in and out of cells, microscope calculations
  • Infection and response — bacteria, viruses, fungi and protists
  • Organisation: enzymes, digestion, the heart, lungs and blood
  • Homeostasis, inheritance, variation and ecosystems
  • The required practicals, and how they get examined

Chemistry — without the dread!

Marks often slip away because students do not fully understand the periodic table's key knowledge and rules.

  • Atomic structure, the periodic table and the three types of bonding
  • Quantitative chemistry: moles, relative formula mass, percentage yield
  • Chemical changes, reactivity, electrolysis and energy changes
  • Rates of reaction, reversible reactions and organic basics
  • Balancing equations until it stops needing thought

Physics, formulas and maths skills — without the switch off!

Equations, graphs and scientific language. Students lose marks when they cannot choose the correct equation, identify its subject or rearrange it accurately.

  • Energy stores, transfers, efficiency and power
  • Forces, motion, distance–time and velocity–time graphs
  • Waves, the electromagnetic spectrum, electricity and magnetism
  • Rearranging any equation, and never losing a unit again
  • Reading data, plotting graphs, describing patterns

Turning knowledge into marks

The session that improves grades fastest, as many marks are lost through insufficient exam practice.

  • Command words: describe, explain, evaluate, compare, suggest
  • A structure for 6-mark questions that scores every time
  • Practical and data questions, done under timed conditions
  • Full past-paper practice with live, worked feedback
  • Rearranging equations following a system that ensures marks are not lost
  • A personal revision plan for the run-up to the real exams

The same four phases, every single week

Predictable structure is what makes difficult science concepts feel manageable. Students always know what is coming next.

  • Connection to prior knowledge, and hooks students' attention.
  • Short tasks, provocative questions or real-world examples connect existing understanding to the lesson topic.
  • It encourages thinking, recalling and predicting, setting the stage for focused learning.
  • Students engage actively with new content through hands-on activities, problem-solving and guided exploration.
  • This phase emphasises inquiry-based learning, letting students wrestle with core concepts and discover understanding rather than passively receive it.
  • Applying their learning to demonstrate understanding.
  • Through discussion, collaborative problem-solving, or creating something that reflects mastery of the lesson objectives.
  • Promoting independence and self-monitoring.
  • Reinforces learning and assesses understanding.
  • Students reflect, complete exit activities and discuss, so knowledge is consolidated and the success criteria are met.
  • Home learning tasks set at this stage, marked and returned with feedback, which also reaches parents.
  • Short video clips to watch between sessions to reinforce key concepts.
  • Revision links and notes provided.

Everything comes with the course

All of this is included in the price — there is nothing extra to buy.

Revision materials

Revision materials for every topic on the course, kept for revision afterwards.

Quizzes

Quizzes to check understanding as you go, so nothing is assumed.

Assessments

Assessments under exam conditions, so the real thing is familiar.

Weekly home learning

A weekly home learning task, with feedback sent to parents.

Rates depend on group size and format — enquire for current prices.

Contact Rod to secure your place

Science in the Daytime

With Rod working from home on Mondays and Tuesdays, daytime sessions present a new opportunity. Before committing to a schedule, we're gauging interest to determine demand and shape the offering accordingly.

Three groups this tends to work for

Home Educated

Families educating at home who want subject-specialist science teaching from someone who knows how the papers are marked.

Flexible Timetables

Anyone whose week does not fit the usual after-school slot — reduced timetables, shift-working parents, part-time arrangements.

International Students

Students studying the curriculum overseas, including those attending international schools or from Armed Forces families.

This page asks rather than tells

Whether daytime sessions run one-to-one or in a small group, which days they land on and what they cost all depend on who comes forward. Rather than invent a timetable and then change it, Rod would rather hear what you need first.

If daytime would suit your family, say so through the enquiry form and mention the days and times that work. If enough people want the same thing, it runs.

The same science, a different hour

Daytime sessions cover the same ground as the rest of SMARTin SCIENCE — Combined Science, Biology, Chemistry and Physics for Years 9 to 11, with exam technique embedded throughout.

item.title: Exam Boards page
item.dc:creator: rod
item.content:encoded:
One curriculum. Four exam boards.

There is one National Science Curriculum in England & Wales, set by the Department for Education — and four different exam boards examining it. Two questions decide how your child should revise: which board they sit, and which course they are on.

Which exam board is your child following?

AQA

Edexcel

Pearson

OCR

Eduqas

WJEC in Wales

The content is the same, however different exam boards organise the content in different ways. The exam papers are also written differently. Knowing which exam board your child is following is vital for exam preparation.

If you do not know, the school will tell you, and it is usually printed on the front of a past paper or a revision guide. Tell Rod when you enquire and the practice questions and past papers used in sessions will support it.

Compare the boards side by side →

Opens Save My Exams, an independent site. Nothing to do with SMARTin SCIENCE — it is simply a clear summary.

Which science course is your child following?

Guided learning hours are the teaching time each qualification is designed to take — the quickest way to see how much extra content the separate sciences carry.

Combined Science

  • 240 guided learning hours
  • Awarded 2 Science GCSEs

Biology

  • 120 guided learning hours
  • Contains all the Biology content covered in Combined Science
  • Plus 40 additional Biology guided learning hours
  • Awarded 1 Biology GCSE

Chemistry

  • 120 guided learning hours
  • Contains all the Chemistry content covered in Combined Science
  • Plus 40 additional Chemistry guided learning hours
  • Awarded 1 Chemistry GCSE

Physics

  • 120 guided learning hours
  • Contains all the Physics content covered in Combined Science
  • Plus 40 additional Physics guided learning hours
  • Awarded 1 Physics GCSE

How SMARTin SCIENCE covers both routes

In most schools across the country, students follow the Combined Science route, with a smaller percentage on the separate science route. If your child is studying the latter, then we will cater for this.

Everyone starts here

Rod will initially cover the content of Combined Science. All students in the country need to cover this content.

Bolt-ons through the year

For those studying the traditional separate sciences, there will be Biology, Chemistry and Physics bolt-ons throughout the year that they can attend, covering the additional content.

Weekend masterclasses

Scheduled throughout the year. Please discuss this option with Rod.

About the masterclasses →

Once you know the board and the course

The four-week course

Biology, chemistry, physics and exam technique — one week each, for Years 9 to 11.

How the weeks run

What happens in each of the four weeks, and when the next block starts.

Questions parents ask

Not sure which board or course your child is on?

item.title: FAQs page
item.dc:creator: rod
item.content:encoded:
The questions parents actually ask

Straight answers about how sessions work, what is covered, and how to start. If yours is not here, just ask — Rod answers his own messages.

Send an enquiry through the website or email Rod directly. Let him know the year group, exam board (if known), and the main challenge. He'll suggest the best approach, explain availability and costs, and arrange a free, no-obligation chat to see if it's the right fit.

Usually not. Be honest with Rod about your current position, and he'll be honest in return. Year 10 offers the most time to improve, while starting in Year 11 means focusing on exam technique and high-value topics. The good news: most students are closer to success than they think.

Start with a free, no-obligation chat. It gives Rod a clear picture of the situation and lets you see whether your child feels comfortable working with him. The right fit matters, as students learn best when they feel confident admitting what they don't understand.

Rod offers both in-person and online tutoring. He's based in Leeds and has limited availability for local face-to-face sessions but works online with students across England and Wales. Online lessons are fully interactive, with shared past papers, live annotations, and real-time explanations. For many families, it's simply the most practical way to maintain consistent weekly support.

Every session follows a clear structure: what we're covering and why, the science explained in a way that makes sense to the student, and practice questions to check understanding. Most sessions finish with targeted work to complete before the next lesson. That consistency helps make challenging science feel manageable

Both work well. One-to-one tuition is tailored to your child's pace, while small groups help students learn from each other's questions and build confidence. Tell Rod what you think would suit your child best, and he'll offer honest advice.

Just a device with a camera and microphone, a reliable internet connection, and a quiet space. A tablet works, but a laptop is usually best. We also recommend having paper and a pen handy, as working through problems on paper helps reinforce learning and makes it easier to spot any misunderstandings.

No. We like to start with cameras on for a quick hello, as it helps build rapport and adds a personal touch. Once the session is underway, your child is welcome to switch their camera off and focus on their work.

We support AQA, Edexcel, OCR & Eduqas. While all GCSE Science courses follow the same national curriculum, each exam board has its own question style and mark scheme. Let Rod know which board your child's school uses, and we'll tailor practice materials accordingly. That exam-specific preparation often makes a bigger difference than parents expect.

Yes. Most teaching focuses on the GCSE Combined Science content, which forms the foundation of all three Separate Sciences. Additional sessions (Bolt Ons) and masterclasses cover the extra Triple Science topics throughout the year.

If your child has significant gaps in a specific subject, Rod may recommend a specialist Biology, Chemistry or Physics tutor instead who may have more time to focus on these areas. The priority is always making sure your child gets the right support.

Required practicals make up around 15% of GCSE Science exam marks, so they are covered in detail. Students learn the methods, variables and science behind each practical, as well as the types of exam questions that commonly appear. Understanding how and why a practical works, rather than simply memorising it, helps students pick up valuable marks in the exam.

Usually, yes, but it's kept focused and manageable. This might be a set of questions, a past-paper task, or a topic your child brings back and explains. The goal isn't to create extra work, but to reinforce learning between sessions, where much of the progress happens.

If your child has a particularly busy week, just let Rod know and the workload can be adjusted accordingly.

You'll often notice the difference before it appears in school reports. A good sign is when your child can confidently explain a topic they previously struggled with. Rod provides honest feedback on what's improving, what still needs work, and where to focus next, so you'll always know how your child is progressing and whether the tuition is making a difference.

Tutoring fees depend on the type of support you need, whether that's one-to-one sessions or small group tuition. Get in touch with a few details and Rod will provide a clear, no-obligation quote tailored to your child's needs.

If your child misses a session, they can catch up by watching the Zoom recording, which is shared in Google Classroom for all students in the group. After completing the recording and any follow-up work, Rod will check that they understand the content. If extra support is needed, a short catch-up session can be arranged at the weekend.

Yes. In-person tutoring is available across the Leeds area, while online sessions are available throughout England and Wales and follow the same high-quality approach as face-to-face teaching.

If you're based overseas and following the English National Curriculum, you're welcome to get in touch. Limited online slots are available on Mondays and Tuesdays for international students.

STEM Workshops and Clubs

STEM stands for Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics. Rather than treating these subjects separately, STEM helps children see how they work together to solve real-world problems.

Through hands-on activities and practical challenges, STEM develops key skills such as problem-solving, critical thinking, creativity and innovation, helping young people build confidence and prepare for future careers and opportunities

Rod runs hands-on STEM workshops for schools, classes and community groups. These one-off practical sessions are designed to spark curiosity, build confidence and bring science to life. Workshops are linked to the annual British Science Week theme, with full details available on the Workshops/Clubs page.

Rod runs hands-on STEM after-school clubs for primary schools, available in blocks throughout the academic year (on a Monday or Tuesday). These engaging sessions encourage curiosity, creativity and problem-solving through practical science, technology, engineering and maths activities. Full details can be found on the Workshops/Clubs page.

Rod runs hands-on STEM holiday clubs across the Leeds area during the school holidays. Designed to be fun, engaging and curiosity-driven, the activities encourage children to explore science, technology, engineering and maths through practical challenges and experiments. For upcoming dates and details, visit the Workshop/Clubs page.

Absolutely! Schools, PTAs, Scouts, Guides, home-education groups and community organisations are welcome to book. Just let us know the number and ages of the children, your location, and what you're looking for. Rod will then get back to you with availability, session options and pricing.

Workshop costs vary depending on the number of children, session length, level of support needed and location. Get in touch with a few details, and Rod will provide a clear, no-obligation quote tailored to your group.

Practical Questions

Yes. Rod holds an Enhanced DBS check and is an experienced teacher with over 20 years' experience working in UK schools.

Parents are always welcome to ask about his current DBS status and safeguarding arrangements when making an enquiry. It's a sensible question, and Rod is happy to discuss it.

Plans can change, and that's understandable. If you need to cancel or reschedule, just let Rod know as soon as possible and he'll do his best to accommodate. Cancellation and rearrangement arrangements will be clearly explained when you book, so there are no surprises.

Still wondering about something?

item.title: Workshops page
item.dc:creator: rod
item.content:encoded:
Science you can get your hands on

Not every student needs a tutor. Some need a reason to like the subject again. STEM workshops, after-school clubs and holiday clubs — run by a former Head of Science who has spent twenty years working out which demonstrations make a room go quiet.

Three ways to bring science to life

Each one is built for a different group and a different amount of time. Tell me which fits and we can shape it from there.

STEM workshops

One-off, hands-on sessions for a class, a year group or a community group. Practical science with a proper question behind it — not a magic show with no explanation.

  • Built around a topic you choose
  • Suits primary through to Key Stage 4
  • In your space or a venue you arrange

After-school clubs

A regular weekly science club through term time. Somewhere the students who love the subject get stretched and the ones who have gone quiet get pulled back in.

  • Runs across a half term or full term
  • Different investigation each week
  • Mixed ability by design

Holiday clubs

Half-term and school-holiday sessions. Longer blocks mean the messier, more memorable experiments that never fit into a single lesson.

  • Half term, Easter and summer
  • Longer sessions, bigger builds
  • Childcare hours that are actually useful

Curiosity first, curriculum second

Get a student genuinely interested and the revision problem mostly solves itself.

They ask the question first

Every session starts with something that does not obviously make sense. The explanation lands harder when a student has already wondered about it.

Real equipment, real method

Measuring properly, recording honestly, and saying what the result actually shows — the habits the required practicals are testing anyway.

Taught, not supervised

Twenty years in front of classes means knowing when to step in and when to let a group struggle productively for another two minutes.

The important thing is to never stop questioning.

What to ask about

Workshops and clubs get shaped around the group, so the details are worth a conversation rather than a price list. When you get in touch, it helps to know:

  • How many students, and roughly what age or year group
  • Where you are — Leeds and West Yorkshire in person, further afield by arrangement
  • What you are hoping for: a one-off, a term of club sessions, or holiday cover
  • Any topic you would like it built around

Rod comes back on availability, what a session would look like, and cost for your group. Schools, PTAs, scout and guide groups, home-education networks and community groups are all welcome to ask.
